cover_hook: A 1-in-100-million ghost lobster went to college
caption_hook: 🦞 A pure white 'ghost' lobster, odds 1 in 100 million, is helping scientists crack the genetics of lobster colours + 3 more wins 👇
question: Describe this news in one emoji 👇
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves weird animals
first_comment: Bonus: the same lab once studied Peaches, a 1-in-30-million orange lobster whose babies came out brown, orange and blue. What colour would you pick? 🦞

stories.headline: A 1-in-100-million white lobster joins a DNA study
stories.summary: Casper, a ghost-white lobster, moved from the Maine State Aquarium to the University of New England, where scientists are scanning 15,000+ genes to learn why some lobsters turn rare colours.
stories.why: Its DNA is collected without harm, and it fills the rarest gap in the colour spectrum.

stories.headline: Syria reopens a 1,500-year-old church after 14 years
stories.summary: After clearing landmines and repairing war and earthquake damage, the UNESCO-listed Saint Simeon complex near Aleppo welcomed visitors again on October 2. It dates to 476–490 AD.
stories.why: It was one of the largest churches in the world until Hagia Sophia.

stories.headline: Antarctica's wind turbines saved 122,000 gallons of diesel
stories.summary: Three turbines bolted to Ross Island's Crater Hill have powered NZ's Scott Base and the US McMurdo Station for 15 years in -30°C cold, avoiding about 1,200 tonnes of CO2.
stories.why: If wind power can survive Antarctica, it can work almost anywhere.

stories.headline: Oman's lonely humpbacks may be a whole new subspecies
stories.summary: Comparing DNA from 2,285 humpbacks worldwide, scientists found Arabian Sea whales have followed their own path for tens of thousands of years. Only about 82 are thought to live off Oman.
stories.why: Official recognition could bring stronger protection for this tiny group.

fun_fact: Pilgrims chipped Saint Simeon's pillar for relics, wearing it from 15 m down to a 3 m stub.
